issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares the attribute `numberOfInscribedStudents` as `int`, but the reference solution declares it as `long` (`private long numberOfInscribedStudents`). This also propagates into the constructor and getter/setter signatures, so students following the UML will implement different method signatures than the reference solution implies.
issues.suggestedFix: Make `numberOfInscribedStudents` consistently typed across UML/problem statement and solution. Prefer changing the solution field, constructor parameter, getter, and setter to `int` to match the UML; alternatively, update the UML/problem statement (and any tests) to use `long` everywhere.

issues.description: In the solution, `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` is declared to return `int`, but it returns `numberOfGuestStudents + numberOfInscribedStudents` where `numberOfInscribedStudents` is `long`. In Java this expression is `long` and cannot be returned as `int` without an explicit cast, so the provided reference solution does not compile as written.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the numeric type inconsistency so the method compiles and matches the spec: either change `numberOfInscribedStudents` to `int` (then the sum is `int`) or change `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` to return `long` and update the UML/problem statement (and dependent methods/tests) accordingly.
